transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

I came in because things have been getting weird at work. I’m a cashier, and I keep getting stuck doing things that don’t really fit what’s happening—like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting. Last week it got bad enough that I got written up, so… I figured I needed to talk to someone.

Right before you start tapping the scanner or freezing up, do you notice a specific worried thought or an uncomfortable feeling that makes you feel like you have to do that action, or does it just happen suddenly without any thought behind it?

It doesn’t feel like a clear worried thought, no. It’s more like I’m at the register and suddenly I’m doing it—tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand just sort of stops over the cash drawer. It doesn’t really match what’s going on, because the customer is right there waiting, and I know it looks strange. I just get stuck.
Do these freezing episodes tend to happen when you're feeling a strong emotion, like laughing hard, getting surprised, or feeling angry, or do they occur regardless of your emotional state?

It seems to happen regardless, as far as I can tell. It’s not like I’m laughing or angry or anything first. I’ll just be at the register, doing my job, and then I get stuck tapping the scanner or my hand freezes over the cash drawer while the customer’s waiting. It doesn’t really fit what’s happening.

Right before the tapping or freezing happens, do you feel a kind of building tension or urge in your body that gets relieved once you do the movement, or does it just happen without any warning sensation at all?

I don’t really notice a buildup or a body urge beforehand. It’s more like I’m just at the register, and then I’m tapping the scanner in a pattern or my hand is stuck over the cash drawer. It feels out of place, especially with the customer waiting, but I don’t feel relief after doing it or anything like that.

During these episodes of tapping or freezing, are you fully aware of what's happening around you and able to remember the episode afterward, or do you ever feel disconnected, spaced out, or have trouble recalling what happened?

I’m aware it’s happening, yes. I can see the customer there and I know I’m supposed to keep moving, but I get stuck tapping the scanner or just holding my hand over the cash drawer. I remember it afterward too—last week it was bad enough that I got written up for it.
Can you tell me how long you've been having these tapping or freezing episodes—did they start when you were a young child, or is this something that began more recently, like in adulthood?
It’s more recent. I don’t remember anything like this when I was a kid. The voices and these more out-of-place moments have been going on for about the last three months.
You mentioned hearing voices—can you tell me more about that? What do the voices say, and when did they start compared to the tapping or freezing episodes?

Most days I hear it. It sounds like a couple of people talking just off to the side of me, or sometimes like someone calling my name from the stockroom. Other times it’ll be something like, “You rang that up wrong,” and I’ll look around, but there’s nobody there. Nobody else seems to hear it.

It started around the same time as the tapping and freezing, maybe all within these last few months.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, new medications, or use of alcohol or recreational drugs around the time these symptoms started?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of any illness or injury that happened around then. I don’t have anything specific I can point to like that.
When these symptoms first started three months ago, did they come on suddenly over just a few days, or did they build up gradually over weeks?

I’m not sure I can pin it down that clearly. It didn’t feel like one specific day where everything changed. I just started noticing things more over a little while, and then it became harder to ignore.
Have you noticed any recent confusion, seizures, fevers, or unusual changes in your heart rate, blood pressure, or sweating around the time these episodes occur?
I haven’t really noticed anything like that. No seizures or fevers that I know of. I don’t think my heart or sweating changes around the episodes, but I’m not really checking it at the time.

Besides hearing these voices, have you noticed any strong beliefs lately that others might see as unusual or not quite true—for example, feeling like people are watching you, plotting against you, or that you have special powers or a special mission?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t felt like I have special powers or anything like that. I don’t really think people are plotting against me. It’s mostly just the voices, as far as I can tell.

Over these past few months, have you noticed yourself pulling away from friends or family, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling like your emotions are flatter or harder to express than before?

Yeah… I think so. I still care about my wife and my kids, but I don’t really have the push to reach out much. Like my son’s away at college, and I know I should call him, but I just… don’t.

I used to meet up with a kayak group sometimes, and I had little repair projects around the house I liked working on. Lately I just let them sit. And when people ask me what’s wrong, I mostly shrug. I can’t really find much to say.

Has anyone in your family ever been diagnosed with schizophrenia or another psychotic illness, or have you personally had any earlier episodes of unusual thinking, hallucinations, or behavior before these last three months?

I don’t know of anyone in my family with anything like that. For me, this is new as far as I can tell. The voices and the stranger, out-of-place moments have really only been going on for about the last three months.

inference.note: No history of medical illness, head injury, substance use, seizures, fever, or autonomic instability to support an organic/catatonic disorder due to a general medical condition, making F06.1 less likely. The combination of prominent catatonic-like motor symptoms (stereotyped tapping, stuporous freezing), auditory hallucinations, and negative symptoms (avolition, blunted affect, social withdrawal) over 3 months without mood symptoms or medical cause supports F20.2 (catatonic schizophrenia) as the primary diagnosis.

opening_question.intent: Establish the primary reason for the visit today
opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits catatonic behaviors (freezing/waxy immobility, stereotyped tapping) without preceding anxiety, tic-like urge, emotional trigger, or dissociation, occurring alongside persistent auditory hallucinations (multiple voices commenting/calling name) and negative symptoms (social withdrawal, anhedonia, blunted affect/avolition). Symptoms have persisted for ~3 months with functional impairment (written up at work), ruling out brief psychotic disorder (<1 month) and favoring schizophrenia, catatonic type given prominence of catatonic motor features. Medical/substance causes were screened and denied, making secondary catatonia (F06.1) or psychotic disorder due to another medical condition less likely. No manic/depressive mood episode reported, arguing against mood disorder with psychotic features.
